Autumn 2 · Week 1 · Behaviour focus · Whole-school assembly

Resilience

It is okay to be stuck. You have comeback moves to keep going.

20 minutes
Think, point, speak or watch.
Nobody is put on the spot.

When a new task feels hard, what does that usually mean?

Discussion / choices: You are learning something new · You can never do it · Everyone else finds it effortless

Key idea: Feeling stuck is a normal part of learning something new — it is a middle step, not a final verdict.

Presenter: Frame resilience as having practical tools when work feels frustrating, not pretending everything is easy.

02 / 10 · Autumn 2 · Week 1 · Behaviour focus · Resilience

The power of “…yet”

1.5–4 min

Watch the scene. Pause at the prediction point and choose what changes after the setback.

Progress is almost never a straight line.

MADE BY MATT · ORIGINAL ANIMATIONOFFLINE

A pupil starts a workshop task confidently, getting the first pieces together. Pause here: the middle piece does not fit and frustration rises. What happens if we add the word '…yet' and pause? Instead of sweeping the work away, the pupil takes three slow breaths, checks the step card, and asks for one pointer. The build comes together. Being stuck was just a middle step, not the end of the story.

PAUSE · PREDICT · REPLAY

03 / 10 · Autumn 2 · Week 1 · Behaviour focus · Resilience

Your four comeback moves

4–6 min

Tap each move in the toolkit to see how it works when you are stuck.

You only need one move to get unstuck.

Discussion / choices: Breathe · Break it down · Try another way · Ask for help

Key idea: Breathe, break it down, try another way, and ask for help are four comeback moves you can use in any lesson.

Presenter: Tap all four options so pupils hear each practical move.

04 / 10 · Autumn 2 · Week 1 · Behaviour focus · Resilience

The bar you cannot empty

6–8.5 min

Tap “Give up” first to see what happens to the bar, then tap the comeback moves to grow it.

Even when work feels tough, your resilience bar never hits zero.

RESILIENCE BAR38% · Keep going

Discussion / choices: Breathe · Break it down · Try another way · Ask for help

Key idea: Stuck is not stopped. Even after a setback, the bar holds at “…yet” and grows with every comeback move.

Presenter: Demonstrate the 'Try Give up' button first so pupils see the bar stop at 16% ('…yet'), then tap the four comeback buttons to reach 100%.

05 / 10 · Autumn 2 · Week 1 · Behaviour focus · Resilience

From stuck to moving again

8.5–10.5 min

Tap the four steps in order to build the comeback routine.

Notice that breathing comes before trying to fix the whole task.

Discussion / choices: KEEP GOING · BREATHE · STUCK · TRY OR ASK

Key idea: STUCK → BREATHE → TRY OR ASK → KEEP GOING.

Presenter: Point out that noticing you are stuck and taking a breath are part of the routine, not a failure.

06 / 10 · Autumn 2 · Week 1 · Behaviour focus · Resilience

Everyone fails on the first try

10.5–12.5 min

Tap each real-life skill to see what happens before it works smoothly.

People who are good at something were once beginners who got it wrong.

Chefs and engineers test recipes and prototypes that go wrong first, then adjust one step at a time.
Every player misses shots and every musician hits wrong notes while practising a new skill.
A rough first draft or a wrong answer shows where to check next — it is how learning happens.

Discussion / choices: Cooking or workshop builds · Games, sport, and music · Writing, maths, and class projects

Key idea: First attempts are meant for learning and adjusting, not for being perfect straight away.

Presenter: Connect to practical lessons in school (kitchen, workshop, art, sport) where testing and adjusting is normal.

07 / 10 · Autumn 2 · Week 1 · Behaviour focus · Resilience

Is asking for help giving up?

12.5–14.5 min

Many people stay stuck because they worry about asking. Tap the three highlighted phrases.

Let's flip a common myth about asking for help.

Asking for help is — it is one of the to get .

NOT GIVING UP: Giving up means walking away; asking means you are still trying to solve it.

SMART MOVE: Experienced learners and workers ask questions early instead of sitting in silence.

NEXT STEP: You can ask 'Could you show me the first step?' or point to the part that feels unclear.

Discussion / choices: not giving up · smartest comeback moves · unstuck and moving

Key idea: Asking for help is not weak or giving up — it is a smart comeback move that gets you moving again.

Presenter: Give pupils low-pressure ways to ask in class, such as pointing to the question or using a help card.

08 / 10 · Autumn 2 · Week 1 · Behaviour focus · Resilience

Quick check: how your brain grows

14.5–16.5 min

True or false: “Making mistakes means you are just not clever.”

Point, show thumbs, or watch.

Discussion / choices: TRUE — clever is fixed · FALSE — mistakes and practice grow the brain · NOT SURE — show the science

Key idea: False. Mistakes and practice are how your brain builds stronger connections.

Presenter: Compare brain pathways to a path across grass: the more often you walk it and adjust, the clearer it becomes.

09 / 10 · Autumn 2 · Week 1 · Behaviour focus · Resilience

Add the word “yet”

16.5–18.5 min

Sort each thought: does it shut the task down, or does it open the next step?

One small word changes what happens next.

Discussion / choices: Sort each thought: does it shut the task down, or does it open the next step?

Key idea: Adding the word 'yet' and choosing one small step keeps the door open when work feels hard.

Presenter: Read each sentence aloud and let the group point or vote before revealing.

10 / 10 · Autumn 2 · Week 1 · Behaviour focus · Resilience

Your comeback move this week

18.5–20 min

Choose the two ideas that help when you hit a tricky task.

Keep your choice private if you prefer.

Discussion / choices: Take three slow breaths and break the task into one small step · Go quiet, push the work away, and give up · Add the word “yet” and ask a trusted adult for the first step

Key idea: When work gets hard: breathe, break it down, try another way, or ask — and add the word 'yet'.

Presenter: End calmly without requiring a public pledge. Remind staff to notice and praise comeback moves in lessons this week.

Word help

resilience
Keeping going, taking a calm pause, or trying another way when a task feels hard.
setback
Something that goes wrong or slows you down on the first attempt.
yet
A short word that reminds you that not knowing how to do something today does not mean you never will.
comeback move
A practical step to use when you are stuck: breathe, break it down, try another way, or ask.

Take a moment

You can look away.
There is no answer needed right now.

Timers and animation are paused.

Teacher desk

20-minute assembly · secondary SEMH

Participation and delivery

Read every prompt and option aloud. Pupils may answer by pointing, thumbs, speaking, or simply watching. Staff operate the board; nobody needs to type. Allow processing time. Do not require eye contact or invite personal disclosures.

Praise effort and specific comeback moves ('you took a breath', 'you broke it down', 'you asked which step comes first') rather than fixed ability ('you are clever'). Never turn resilience into a public test in front of the hall.
